messages:
maya: Heads-up — I found a weird token-accounting gap on the staging invoice for last night's canary. We saw ~3.5k tokens charged but only ~1.2k bytes streamed to the client.
chris: That sounds like the toolcall TTL evictions we were worried about? Which flow?
maya: Yeah, user request -> streaming chunks -> runtime makes a toolcall to web_search -> tool responds, we stream partial answer, then the long tail of the tool response got truncated by our truncation path when the KV cache evicted the call context. Billing shows the full attempted tokens for the tool response (including the truncated tail) and also double-counted when the request retried the toolcall.
ranjit: Do we charge on 'attempted tokens' or 'delivered tokens' currently? I thought we finalize charges after the response completes.
sylvia: Short answer: we emit provisional token events during streaming (for real-time quota/limits) and then a finalization event on completion. Problem is: retries inside the runtime (idempotent or not) can generate multiple provisional events but the finalization hook sometimes never reconciles correctly when truncation/eviction occurs.
ken: Can you paste the event log snippet?
maya: Sure — simplified:
```
{event: "tokens_provisional", count: 3200, req_id: "r-abc"}
{event: "tokens_provisional", count: 800, req_id: "r-abc", retry: 1}
{event: "tokens_final", count: 1200, req_id: "r-abc"}
```
So ledger ends up summing provisional events unless the final event explicitly zeroes out or reconciles.
chris: Ugh. So the provisional stream is useful for quota enforcement but we never reliably deduct provisional overshoots for truncated responses or KV-evicted toolcalls.
ranjit: Two orthogonal issues: (1) retries creating duplicate provisional entries, (2) finalization missing or not idempotent when truncation occurs. We should make finalization strongly idempotent and reference the provisional sequence numbers.
sylvia: Also console/quotas UX: product expects quotas displayed as "committed usage" vs "real-time usage". Right now UI shows the sum of provisionals which scares customers. Should surface provisional vs committed separately.
billing-bot: cc @billing-team — observed a 0.8% delta between provisional and invoiced tokens last 24h on staging cluster-3.
ken: For quick mitigation I propose: (A) When a toolcall starts, assign a stable toolcall-id and attach it to all provisional events; (B) on retries, check the idempotency key to avoid emitting new provisional tokens; (C) only mark provisional as billable after toolcall finalization or after a configurable grace window (e.g., 2s) if finalization never happens.
maya: I like (A)+(B). (C) worries me for tail latency-sensitive customers though — we need quotas to enforce hard caps in real-time. Maybe keep provisional for enforcement but mark them as non-billable until finalized.
chris: Implementation detail: our current token meter writes two types into kafka: meter.provisional and meter.final. Change needed: include fields {toolcall_id, provisional_seq, finalized: boolean, basis: "delivered|attempted|truncated"}. Final events must include which provisionals they reconcile.
ranjit: We also need a reconciliation job that runs periodically to reclassify orphaned provisionals (older than TTL and never finalized) and either purge or finalize them as truncated with proper attribution. That job should emit a reconciliation audit log so finance can trace.
sylvia: UX asks: show provisional delta in the console and add an explain button "Why do provisional tokens differ from invoice?" with a short blurb. Also add a recent-reconciliations view.
ken: Telemetry plan: track metric provisional_vs_final_ratio per model/per-route, count of provisional events with missing finalization, and % of reconciliations that change invoice. Add alert threshold at 0.5% delta for prod.
maya: Edge case: streaming + client disconnect mid-toolcall. How do we bill? Current behavior: we finalize on server completion, which counts full tool response even if client disconnected after first chunk. I think we should bill for server work performed (we executed tokens) but mark the delivered tokens separately in console. Finance prefers billing for consumed compute (so server-side tokens).
chris: Agree, but clarify in docs and show both numbers. Billing should be for server tokens. UI: delivered_tokens vs server_tokens.
ranjit: Okay action items:
- Ranjit: PR to add toolcall_id + provisional_seq to meter messages and make finalization idempotent by referencing seqs. (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- Maya: Add a reconciliation lambda to mark orphaned provisionals as truncated/settled and emit audit records. (ETA: Tue)
- Sylvia: Console change: add provisional vs committed toggle and explain text. (ETA: next sprint)
- Ken: Add telemetry alerts and a small dashboard for provisional_vs_final_ratio. (ETA: 2 days)
chris: Billing/finance, can you confirm acceptable reconciliation semantics? (cc @billing-bot)
billing-bot: From finance: we need the audit exports to match invoiced numbers. Reclassifying provisionals as "truncated" is fine but must be traceable to request IDs and show timestamps.
maya: One more note: consider not emitting provisional events during speculative retries inside runtime for the same logical request (keep provisional only for the active in-flight toolcall). That should stop most dupes.
ranjit: Yeah, will add a small in-memory guard keyed by toolcall_id in the runtime. If the retry sees the same id, we skip provisional emission.
sylvia: Thanks team. This should clean up the scary console spikes.
ken: I'll create the follow-up ticket and link PRs. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-canary: runtime patch r-commit-482 scheduled at 2026-03-19T02:00Z
chris: Great — monitor provisional_vs_final_ratio closely during canary and rollback if it goes above 1%.
maya: I'll watch invoices and post here if anything odd shows up.
